name: Lutetium Lu 177 Dotatate (PRRT) - GI/pancreatic NET

biomarkers.SSTR: somatostatin-receptor (SSTR) positive on SSTR-PET/CT or SSTR-PET/MRI (tumor uptake at least equal to normal liver background)
biomarkers.note: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with lutetium Lu 177 dotatate requires well-differentiated, SSTR-positive disease (SSTR-PET uptake threshold). Randomized data (NETTER-1) suggest superior PFS and response versus small molecules. PRRT should generally be avoided if GFR is below 30 mL/min. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors, Principles of PRRT (NE-J), and DeVita 12th ed.

lineOfTherapy: for advanced well-differentiated SSTR-positive NET, including after progression on somatostatin analogues; first-line PRRT may be considered in selected patients

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: well-differentiated NET with SSTR-positive imaging (tumor uptake at least equal to normal liver on SSTR-PET)
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v1.2026, neuroendocrine line 662 (SSTR expression detected by SSTR-PET/CT or SSTR-PET/MRI; threshold for PRRT is tumor uptake)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: adequate renal function (avoid PRRT if GFR below 30; use with caution otherwise)
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v1.2026, neuroendocrine line 664 (PRRT should generally be avoided in patients with GFR below 30)

exclusionCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors

drugs.name: Lutetium Lu 177 dotatate

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors
provenance.locator: neuroendocrine line 696 (Lutetium Lu 177 dotatate administered via peripheral IV at a dose of 200 mCi over 30 to 40 minutes every 8 weeks for a total of 4)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) NET v1.2026 (neuroendocrine line 696) and DeVita 12th ed. (NETTER-1, four cycles every 8 weeks). DOSE: 200 mCi (7.4 GBq) IV over 30 to 40 minutes, every 8 weeks, for a total of 4 administrations. UNIT NOTE: the true unit is millicuries (mCi) of radioactivity; unit is recorded as mCi (the sourced activity is 200 mCi = 7.4 GBq); this is NOT a VERIFY (the dose is source-established). Radioligand: no ISMP tall-man form. Amino acid solution is co-administered for renal protection (30 minutes before, concurrently, and 3 hours after, NCCN line 699).

premedications.name: Renal-protective amino acid infusion
premedications.notes: Administer amino acid solution 30 minutes before, concurrently with, and 3 hours after each lutetium Lu 177 dotatate dose (NCCN line 699); aggressive antiemetic prophylaxis when nonselective amino acid solutions are used (NCCN line 713).

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: Provide before and during amino acid and lutetium Lu 177 dotatate infusion.

supportiveCare: Hold short-acting octreotide at least 24 hours before each lutetium Lu 177 dotatate dose; long-acting SSA (octreotide LAR or lanreotide) may be given 4 to 24 hours after each PRRT dose (NCCN lines 692, 731).
Renal protection with amino acid co-infusion is mandatory (NCCN line 699).
PRRT should generally be avoided if GFR is below 30 mL/min (NCCN line 664).

monitoring: renal function (creatinine/GFR) before each dose - nephrotoxicity risk despite amino acid protection
CBC (myelosuppression; risk of therapy-related myeloid neoplasm) before each dose and on follow-up

doseModificationRules.text: Hold, dose-reduce, or discontinue PRRT per labeling and radiation-safety protocol; obtain clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: NETTER-1: four cycles of Lu 177 dotatate given every 8 weeks followed by octreotide LAR, demonstrating a robust PFS benefit in midgut NET

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors
guideline.locator: Principles of PRRT with Lutetium Lu 177 Dotatate (NE-J); neuroendocrine lines 662 (SSTR threshold), 664 (avoid if GFR below 30), 696 (200 mCi over 30 to 40 minutes every 8 weeks for a total of 4), 699 (amino acid co-infusion), 692 and 731 (SSA timing)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for lutetium Lu 177 dotatate PRRT in well-differentiated, SSTR-positive GI/pancreatic NET (disease #30). The radioligand dose - 200 mCi (7.4 GBq) IV over 30 to 40 minutes every 8 weeks for 4 total administrations - is dose-grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) NET v1.2026 (neuroendocrine line 696) and DeVita 12th ed. (NETTER-1). The unit is recorded as mCi (200 mCi = 7.4 GBq); the dose is source-established, so no field is set to VERIFY. Biomarker gates: well-differentiated NET that is SSTR-positive on SSTR-PET (uptake at least equal to liver); PRRT avoided if GFR below 30 (exclusion). Mandatory renal-protective amino acid co-infusion and SSA timing rules are captured. No dose was invented or inferred. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
